Thirty-two native paid-action cases include both stack-copy modes for all 13 Licids and six timed/layered animation cases. One synthetic contract checks canonical aliases and independent collections.
Eighteen packaged witnesses test the 13 paid reversals and five other animations. Payment-count expectations were checked against retained Oracle text.
Licids have friendly controlled targets after a native turn cycle. Timed fixtures begin in postcombat main; phase hooks offer no response priority.
These paths do not certify every Licid granted ability, hostile-target control interaction, all source/target zone transitions or animation overlap.
